title: ‘The Birthday Party’ Review: A Dazzlingly Melancholy Monica Bellucci Powers Léa Mysius’ Predictable but Superbly Directed Home Invasion Thriller
summary: A birthday celebration turns into hell on Earth in this tensely crafted thriller where the production values elevate conventional material.

title: ‘Once Upon a Time in Harlem’: Why William Greaves Didn’t Finish What He Considered His Most Important Film
summary: Cannes: The groundbreaking director believed the 1972 Harlem Renaissance gathering was the best thing he’d ever shot, but his son David discusses finishing the film after he died.

title: Why Director Boots Riley Embraced ‘Jankiness’ and an Indie Spirit to Make ‘I Love Boosters’
summary: Writer and director Boots Riley tells IndieWire why "pulling a Peter Greenaway" is important to creating the visual stories he wants to tell.

title: Who Will Win the Cannes Film Festival Palme d’Or?
summary: Cannes: We rank the contenders out of the 2026 edition so far, with "Minotaur," "The Black Ball," "Paper Tiger," "All of a Sudden," "Fatherland," and even the sci-fi monster movie "Hope" on the up.

title: Audiences Expecting an AI Dystopia in ‘Sheep in the Box’ Get Something Much Stranger from Hirokazu Koreeda
summary: The "Shoplifters" Palme d'Or-winner tells IndieWire about his new film at a pivotal moment for Japan at Cannes.

title: How Do We Adapt to the Age of AI While ‘Protecting the Soul’ of Cinema?
summary: The New Playbook for Independent Film: From Financing to Distribution in the Age of AI, presented by Clever Caboose, offered Cannes attendees a primer in creating art in a data-driven world. Watch the full panel.

title: The American Pavilion Presented by IndieWire Announces Winners of the 2026 Emerging Filmmaker Showcase at Cannes
summary: The showcase, presented by Gold House, honored some of the year's best filmmaking from students and early career professionals.

title: How World-Class Filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev Came Back to Life for ‘Minotaur’
summary: The director almost died from complications of COVID. But he recovered, slowly, and tells IndieWire how he rediscovered the joy of filmmaking outside his native Russia with Competition Contender "Minotaur."

title: Critic’s Notebook: The Best Films at Cannes 2026 Challenged Us to Redraw Our Relationship to Reality
summary: "Club Kid," "Camp Miasma," and "Minotaur" may not have a lot in common, but they all stood out from a weak lineup for a similar reason.

title: ‘Mating Season’ Review: Nick Kroll’s Animated Netflix Comedy Is Too Much and Too Little Like ‘Big Mouth’
summary: The creators of the acclaimed comedy about surviving adolescence return with a similar series set in the animal kingdom, where four furry friends navigate love, sex, and survival — among other primal instincts.

title: ‘Coward’ Review: Lukas Dhont’s Study of the Gay Yearning Between Beautiful WWI Soldiers Is His Best Film Yet
summary: "Coward' is yet another story of queer repression and suffering from the director of "Girl" and "Close," and it's often breathtaking, whether in battle or the bedroom, even if too decorous to really steal your heart away.

title: ‘How We Grieve’ Trailer: PBS Doc Series Produced by Rachel Bloom Preps Us for Our Turn in the Urn
summary: Exclusive: Filmmakers and siblings Meghan and Justin Ross' latest project explores how people process their fear of the end and why we avoid talking about it — particularly in an Arab family like theirs.
